2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Long-context language models place acute pressure on the key--value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length \cite{kwon-sosp2023, pope-mlsys2023}.

Recent evaluations show that reasoning capabilities degrade disproportionately under compound compression \cite{unicomp-2026}, and that per-dimension safe zones intersect to form a smaller joint safe region \cite{phase-transition-compression-2026}.

To test whether the phase-modulated severity pattern extends beyond the Qwen2 architecture, we replicate the full experiment on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, 8B parameters; $n{=}250$, MATH-500) under both importance-based and random eviction at $s \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30\}$. Table~\ref{tab:llama-cross-arch} reports per-phase interaction indices for all 8 conditions.

The phase gradient replicates fully: importance-based eviction yields low/high ratios of $49{\times}$ to $22{\times}$, while random eviction yields $1.2$--$1.5{\times}$, producing a strategy${\times}$phase gradient ratio of $15$--$33{\times}$ that matches the Qwen2-family pattern. The absolute magnitude is architecture-dependent (${\sim}26{\times}$ smaller than Qwen2 models), consistent with architecture-specific attention head specialization, but the qualitative structure is preserved.

A key observation: at $s{=}0.30$, the low-phase absolute II values under importance ($1.465$) and random ($1.461$) eviction are nearly identical, yet phase gradients diverge by $18{\times}$ ($22{\times}$ vs.\ $1.21{\times}$). This confirms that the phase gradient is the informative compound interaction signature, structurally coupled to the scoring mechanism rather than to compression magnitude.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-architecture validation: per-phase II on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, $n{=}250$, MATH-500). Low/High: ratio of low-phase to high-phase median II.}
\label{tab:llama-cross-arch}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
\toprule
$s$ & Strategy & $\widetilde{\mathrm{II}}_{\textit{high}}$ & $\widetilde{\mathrm{II}}_{\textit{low}}$ & Low/High & Gradient ratio \\
\midrule
0.15 & Importance & $0.001$ & $0.049$ & $49{\times}$ & \multirow{2}{*}{$33{\times}$} \\
0.15 & Random     & $0.055$ & $0.072$ & $1.47{\times}$ & \\
\addlinespace
0.20 & Importance & $0.007$ & $0.172$ & $25{\times}$ & \multirow{2}{*}{$18{\times}$} \\
0.20 & Random     & $0.164$ & $0.214$ & $1.36{\times}$ & \\
\addlinespace
0.25 & Importance & $0.019$ & $0.415$ & $23{\times}$ & \multirow{2}{*}{$18{\times}$} \\
0.25 & Random     & $0.435$ & $0.563$ & $1.27{\times}$ & \\
\addlinespace
0.30 & Importance & $0.032$ & $0.809$ & $22{\times}$ & \multirow{2}{*}{$18{\times}$} \\
0.30 & Random     & $0.837$ & $1.044$ & $1.21{\times}$ & \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Magnitude comparison.}
LLaMA interaction indices are approximately $26{\times}$ smaller than those on Qwen2-architecture models at matched sparsity. This gap likely reflects differences in attention head specialization between MHA (Qwen2, 28 heads) and GQA (LLaMA, 32 heads with 8 KV groups). Despite this magnitude difference, the strategy specificity replicates ($15$--$33{\times}$ on LLaMA vs.\ $15$--$17{\times}$ on DeepSeek and $2.7$--$3.5{\times}$ on Qwen), confirming that the phase-gated interaction pattern is architecture-general.

To test whether the phase-modulated severity pattern extends beyond the Qwen2 architecture, we replicate the full experiment on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, 8B parameters; $n{=}250$, MATH-500) under both importance-based and random eviction at $s \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30\}$. Table~\ref{tab:llama-cross-arch} reports paired median differences and effect sizes for all 8 conditions.

The within-importance phase gradient replicates with large effect sizes: $\Delta$ rises monotonically from $0.050$ ($s{=}0.15$, $d_z{=}0.81$) to $0.695$ ($s{=}0.30$, $d_z{=}1.15$), all $p < 10^{-29}$. An architecture-specific difference emerges in strategy specificity: random eviction on LLaMA also exhibits statistically significant phase gradients at all four sparsity levels ($\Delta{=}0.025$--$0.271$; $d_z{=}0.41$--$0.46$; all $p < 10^{-12}$), unlike DeepSeek and Qwen where random eviction is non-significant at $s \leq 0.20$. The importance/random $\Delta$ ratio on LLaMA is $2.0$--$2.6{\times}$, substantially weaker than the $15$--$17{\times}$ observed on DeepSeek.

Dose-response monotonicity holds for both strategies across all sparsity levels, supporting the phase gradient as an architecture-general phenomenon. The reduced strategy specificity on LLaMA suggests that GQA's grouped key-value structure partially preserves importance score quality under head pruning, attenuating the discrimination collapse that drives strategy divergence on MHA architectures.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-architecture validation: paired median difference ($\Delta$) and effect size ($d_z$) on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, $n{=}250$, MATH-500). All conditions are monotonic.}
\label{tab:llama-cross-arch}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llccc@{}}
\toprule
$s$ & Strategy & $\Delta$ & $d_z$ & $p$ \\
\midrule
0.15 & Importance & $0.050$ & $0.814$ & $1.4 \times 10^{-29}$ \\
0.15 & Random     & $0.025$ & $0.436$ & $9.3 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
\addlinespace
0.20 & Importance & $0.159$ & $1.010$ & $8.9 \times 10^{-35}$ \\
0.20 & Random     & $0.065$ & $0.459$ & $3.6 \times 10^{-15}$ \\
\addlinespace
0.25 & Importance & $0.376$ & $1.115$ & $4.3 \times 10^{-39}$ \\
0.25 & Random     & $0.184$ & $0.424$ & $3.8 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
\addlinespace
0.30 & Importance & $0.695$ & $1.150$ & $1.5 \times 10^{-40}$ \\
0.30 & Random     & $0.271$ & $0.410$ & $6.0 \times 10^{-12}$ \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\footnotesize Imp/Rand $\Delta$ ratio: $2.0$--$2.6{\times}$ (cf.\ $15$--$17{\times}$ on DeepSeek).}
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Magnitude comparison.}
LLaMA interaction magnitudes are approximately $7$--$12{\times}$ smaller than Qwen2-architecture models at matched sparsity. This gap likely reflects differences in attention head specialization between MHA (Qwen2, 28 heads) and GQA (LLaMA, 32 heads with 8 KV groups). The phase gradient direction and dose-response monotonicity replicate, supporting the architecture-generality of phase-modulated compound interaction. Strategy specificity, however, is weaker ($2.0$--$2.6{\times}$ on LLaMA vs.\ $15$--$17{\times}$ on DeepSeek), indicating that the magnitude of strategy${\times}$phase interaction depends on architectural factors governing importance score stability under pruning.

6:The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($\Delta$: $0.07 \to 3.16$; $\rho{=}1.0$), shows consistent phase gradient direction on GSM8K for both models, and generalizes to LlamaForCausalLM ($n{=}250$; strategy${\times}$phase gradient ratio of $15$--$33{\times}$ replicates despite ${\sim}26{\times}$ smaller absolute magnitude).

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Compound sparsity---simultaneously pruning attention heads and evicting KV cache entries---is essential for efficient LLM inference but produces super-additive quality degradation whose structure is poorly understood.
3	We find that compound sparsity severity is not a fixed constant but an emergent property of the interaction among eviction strategy, reasoning phase, and sparsity level.
4	On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (MATH-500), importance-based eviction exhibits a monotonically increasing phase--severity gradient: the paired median difference $\Delta$ rises from $0.39$ at sparsity $s{=}0.15$ to $8.48$ at $s{=}0.30$ (Spearman $\rho{=}1.0$; all Bonferroni-corrected $p < 0.005$).
5	Random eviction develops a detectable gradient only above $s \approx 0.20$, at $2.7$--$17{\times}$ smaller magnitude.
6	The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($\Delta$: $0.07 \to 3.16$; $\rho{=}1.0$), shows consistent phase gradient direction on GSM8K for both models, and generalizes to LlamaForCausalLM ($n{=}250$; strategy${\times}$phase gradient ratio of $15$--$33{\times}$ replicates despite ${\sim}26{\times}$ smaller absolute magnitude).
7	Per-phase Gini analysis identifies \emph{importance discrimination collapse}---the degeneration of head importance scores toward uniformity under compound stress---as a correlational diagnostic of this severity divergence.
8	Prior work characterizes compound degradation as phase-agnostic; we show that phase modulates severity by $15$--$17{\times}$ on DeepSeek and $2.7$--$3.5{\times}$ on Qwen. These findings establish phase-gated analysis---decomposing compound severity by reasoning phase and eviction strategy---as a principled diagnostic framework, with direct implications for phase-aware budget allocation in inference systems.
9	\end{abstract}

35	\paragraph{Architectural scope.}
36	Our two models---DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct---share the Qwen2ForCausalLM architecture.
37	The cross-training-paradigm replication (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}) suggests that the findings are not artifacts of a single model's weights, though both models share the same Qwen2ForCausalLM architecture.
38	Pilot cross-architecture evidence from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, \S\ref{sec:cross-arch}, Appendix~\ref{app:cross-arch}) suggests qualitatively consistent within-importance phase gradients ($d_z \sim 1.0$) but a substantially weaker strategy $\times$ phase interaction than in Qwen2-based architectures; random pruning also exhibits a non-trivial phase gradient on LLaMA, reducing the strategy contrast. This preliminary evidence ($s{=}0.30$ Wilcoxon $p_{\text{Bonf}}{=}0.029$; $s \leq 0.25$ non-significant) is consistent with the qualitative pattern extending beyond Qwen2 but is insufficient for definitive cross-architecture claims; quantitative impact is architecture-dependent. Comprehensive cross-architecture validation across more diverse designs (e.g., Mistral, multi-latent attention architectures) and scales remains an important next step.
39	
40	
41	\paragraph{Task coverage.}
42	We evaluate exclusively on MATH-500, a mathematical reasoning benchmark.
43	Different reasoning tasks---code generation, commonsense reasoning, multi-hop question answering---may induce different phase structures with different sparsity distributions, potentially altering the severity gradient profile.
44	Generalizing the phase-strategy interaction to broader reasoning domains is an important next step.

90	\subsection{Cross-Architecture Validation}
91	\label{sec:cross-arch}
92	
93	Cross-architecture validation on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, $n{=}250$, MATH-500) supports the generality of phase-modulated compound interaction beyond the Qwen2 architecture family. Under importance-based eviction, the paired median difference $\Delta$ rises monotonically from $0.050$ ($s{=}0.15$) to $0.695$ ($s{=}0.30$), with large effect sizes throughout ($d_z{=}0.81$--$1.15$; all $p < 10^{-29}$; Table~\ref{tab:llama-cross-arch}).
94	
95	A key architectural difference emerges in strategy specificity. On LLaMA, random eviction also exhibits significant phase gradients ($\Delta{=}0.025$--$0.271$; $d_z{=}0.41$--$0.46$; all $p < 10^{-12}$), unlike DeepSeek and Qwen where random is non-significant at $s \leq 0.20$. The importance/random $\Delta$ ratio is $2.0$--$2.6{\times}$ on LLaMA, substantially weaker than the $15$--$17{\times}$ observed on DeepSeek. Dose-response monotonicity holds for both strategies (all conditions monotonic). This indicates that the phase gradient itself is architecture-general, while the degree of strategy specificity is architecture-dependent, likely reflecting differences between GQA (LLaMA, 32 heads with 8 KV groups) and MHA (Qwen2, 28 heads) in how head pruning differentially disrupts importance scoring.
96	
97	Absolute interaction magnitudes are approximately $7$--$12{\times}$ smaller than Qwen2-family models at matched sparsity, consistent with architecture-specific attention head specialization patterns. Full per-condition breakdowns appear in Appendix~\ref{app:cross-arch}.
98

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Compound sparsity---simultaneously pruning attention heads and evicting KV cache entries---is essential for efficient LLM inference but produces super-additive quality degradation whose structure is poorly understood.
3	We find that compound sparsity severity is not a fixed constant but an emergent property of the interaction among eviction strategy, reasoning phase, and sparsity level.
4	On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (MATH-500), importance-based eviction exhibits a monotonically increasing phase--severity gradient: the paired median difference $\Delta$ rises from $0.39$ at sparsity $s{=}0.15$ to $8.48$ at $s{=}0.30$ (Spearman $\rho{=}1.0$; all Bonferroni-corrected $p < 0.005$).
5	Random eviction develops a detectable gradient only above $s \approx 0.20$, at $2.7$--$17{\times}$ smaller magnitude.
6	The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($\Delta$: $0.07 \to 3.16$; $\rho{=}1.0$), shows consistent phase gradient direction on GSM8K for both models, and generalizes to LlamaForCausalLM ($n{=}250$; importance phase gradient $d_z{=}0.81$--$1.15$, all $p < 10^{-29}$; strategy specificity architecture-dependent).
7	Per-phase Gini analysis identifies \emph{importance discrimination collapse}---the degeneration of head importance scores toward uniformity under compound stress---as a correlational diagnostic of this severity divergence.
8	Prior work characterizes compound degradation as phase-agnostic; we show that phase modulates severity by $15$--$17{\times}$ on DeepSeek and $2.7$--$3.5{\times}$ on Qwen. These findings establish phase-gated analysis---decomposing compound severity by reasoning phase and eviction strategy---as a principled diagnostic framework, with direct implications for phase-aware budget allocation in inference systems.
9	\end{abstract}
